title: How Plants Eat
summary: This lesson explores photosynthesis, the process by which plants make food. Students will examine how chlorophyll, sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water interact to produce glucose and release oxygen.

sections.text: Scene: A green leaf is shown with chlorophyll inside, capturing sunlight to begin the food-making process. I wonder...? Answer: Chlorophyll in leaves captures sunlight to help plants make food.
Scene: A diagram displays carbon dioxide entering through stomata and water being absorbed through roots. I wonder...? Answer: Plants take in carbon dioxide through stomata and water through roots.

Scene: The Calvin cycle is illustrated converting light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar, while glucose is produced and oxygen is released. I wonder...? Answer: They produce glucose, release oxygen, and use the Calvin cycle to convert light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.

learning_objectives: Explain how plants make food using photosynthesis.
Describe the role of chlorophyll, stomata, and roots in capturing light, carbon dioxide, and water.
Identify the products of photosynthesis including glucose, oxygen, and stored chemical energy.

vocabulary.definition: A substance in leaves that captures sunlight.
Structures through which plants take in carbon dioxide.
The process that converts light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar.
